title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-harper-evans-inference-contract
content:
Notes / scratchpad for incoming customer contract (inference platform). Informal working notes and negotiation playbook.

Objectives:
- Protect Customer Data + Model Outputs (no vendor training on customer data unless explicit opt-in).
- Clear SLA for availability and latency with remediation credits and termination rights for sustained breaches.
- Ensure customer retains ownership of outputs; restrict vendor IP claims.
- KMS/BYOK where required; keys must not be exported or used for training.
- Reasonable liability cap with carveouts for willful misconduct, fraud, and IP infringement.

Redlines / clauses to watch:
1) Data use / training ban: require explicit clause: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data or Model Outputs to train, tune, benchmark, or otherwise improve Vendor models without Customer's prior written consent." Watch for permissive language ("derive insights" / "aggregate, de-identified data"). If they insist on telemetry, limit to operational metrics, anonymized, 30d retention, and opt-out.

2) Ownership of outputs: Customer retains all rights to Model Outputs and any application-specific artifacts. Vendor must grant Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use outputs; vendor shall not assert ownership.

3) IP / licensing: push for explicit perpetual license to outputs. If vendor demands any rights to outputs, require narrow, time-boxed license tied to a paid program.

4) Confidentiality / data residency: include residency commitments for regulated customers (e.g., EU-only storage). Add obligation to notify and remediate any data transfers.

5) KMS/HSM / key control: for Private deployments require BYOK integration and that vendor never exports keys. For Hosted, require SSE-C or customer-managed key option, or contractual guarantee that keys will not be used for training or re-encryption for other customers.

6) Logs / telemetry retention: default debug logs 30d; production traces 90d unless extended via SOW. Prohibit long-term retention of raw customer inputs without explicit consent; sensitive fields must be redacted.

7) SLA: separate availability and latency. Example anchors: Hosted availability 99.9% monthly; Dedicated commit 99.95%. Remedies: service credits, escalation path, and right to terminate for sustained <99% for two consecutive months. Define measurement method, reporting, and carveouts for maintenance/force majeure. For latency (p95 token latency), define measurement endpoint, sampling method, and exclusion windows.

8) Maintenance windows: require >=72h notice for non-emergency maintenance impacting capacity; allow emergency maintenance with post-notice and reasonable mitigation.

9) Security / patching: vendor to apply critical security patches within 14 days and provide CVE notifications. For private/on-prem, clearly allocate patching responsibility and cadence.

10) Indemnities & liability cap: recommend target cap = max(3x fees in prior 12 months, $10M) — confirm with Finance. Carveouts: gross negligence, willful misconduct, IP infringement. Discuss stance on regulatory fines (often excluded; flag for negotiation).

11) Warranties / disclaimers: vendor will disclaim model correctness/hallucinations — expect resistance to warranty around output accuracy. Require warranties for availability, security, and compliance obligations. For hallucination risk, negotiate a joint remediation runbook and timely vendor support for high-severity incidents.

12) Training / benchmarking: explicitly prohibit use of Customer Data for public benchmarks or internal model evaluation without consent. If vendor requests, channel into separate paid, time-limited program with clear data handling and ROI.

13) Export controls & restricted use: include representations supporting export compliance and vendor obligation to suspend service where required, with mitigation plan and notice.

14) Subprocessors / affiliates: require prior notice for material new subprocessors and allow customer opt-out or escalation for regulated customers. Maintain subprocessor list in an appendix.

15) Audit / right to audit: provide SOC 2 / ISO reports routinely; for sensitive customers include virtual/on-site audit rights per SOW.

Negotiation playbook for Sales/Commercial:
- Data usage: if vendor insists on broad telemetry rights, offer narrow ops metrics (anonymized) with 30d retention and opt-out.
- Liability cap: tie to committed spend (3x prior 12 months) and retain carveouts.
- SLA remedies: prefer service credits + escalation; terminate only for repeated material failures.
- Training rights: offer optional paid data-sharing/training program with explicit term, controls, and compensation.

Open items / TODOs:
- Confirm acceptable liability cap range with Finance (floor/ceiling).
- Get infra input on BYOK/BYOK-for-hosted feasibility and template language.
- Decide SLO measurement ownership: propose independent monitoring (customer agent + vendor logs).
- Draft private-deployment support & patch SLA template with release-engineering and SRE.
- Create standard data deletion attestation process for sales to reference.

Small flags for Sales:
- Capture committed spend window for liability calculations.
- If customer asks for data deletion cert, confirm process and attestation timeline before promising.

Negotiation sweeteners (for upsell): limited paid training opt-in, premium support for dedicated pools, extended log retention as a billable add-on.

Next steps: convert to a redline once liability numbers confirmed and infra validates BYOK path. Share with Jordan/Maya/Evelyn for comments and then produce a formal redline against the customer's latest draft.
